title: Jev AI Explained: Why This Viral Model Refuses to Talk
description:
Jev AI explained: Jev, from the San Francisco lab TypeSafe, is a "System One" AI model that doesn't chat, write or explain. It only makes decisions, with probabilities.

How it works
• You give it a state (text or JSON) and typed questions. It answers with calibrated probabilities instead of text.
• Three question types: Choice (pick one option), Score (a value on a scale) and Noul (yes or no, and how sure).
• The confidence decides when your software acts on its own and when a person takes over.
• The name comes from System 1 in Daniel Kahneman's Thinking, Fast and Slow: fast, intuitive judgment.

Speed and price (TypeSafe's own claims)
• 193.6x faster and 444.6x cheaper than LLMs on TypeSafe's System One workflow test (0.114 s and $0.000081 against 8.566 s and $0.013880).
• $42 per billion input tokens; output tokens are free.

Seen in the wild
Routing support tickets, guarding what AI agents may run, and even a Doom demo (reported by The Register).

The catch
It only answers the questions you ask, from the options you give, and it can still be wrong: its calibration holds across many answers, not every single one. It's closed (API only, no weights), and the speed and cost figures come from the company, not an independent benchmark.
